review_items.rationale: Reviewed fixed artifact 4f9d225f6add4020be1ff161487371e2 v2, its initialization diff, unchanged Claim C-verify-eligible v1 and implication predicate, and raw CheckRun 7799a8fae1504918a40da305dff580be. Earlier source/observation analysis in cd296233f8cf4a0481224b78f2bb0315 is reused only for unchanged portions. The increment bootstraps only voter a, checks its stored index is 1 and all three joining stores are empty, then constructs all nodes. Actual voter RPC handlers on empty joining nodes are explicitly permitted by requestVote, advance their term, check history and persist votes. runCandidate must actually reach Leader before prepared is emitted. Thus the single-bootstrap caller-duty issue is repaired, without excluding the nonvoter callback premise. At registration the leader still owns the fixed three-voter/one-nonvoter configuration. Voter append traffic is blocked before any replication starts, no old append replies exist, and actual nonvoter handlers supply responses through InmemTransport. Fresh raw events show prepared term=2, bootstrap_nodes=1, empty_joining_nodes=3, followed by admitted and completed result for verify-1. Result success=true, eligible_voter_support=1, quorum=2, eligible_voter_quorum=false, positive_append_responses={n:1}; state remains Leader term 2. The wrapper increments protected counters before returning to protocol workers; no other-voter response can be omitted by a sampling race because all such calls are blocked for the entire replication tenure. Election votes are separate authority-acquisition messages and are not callbacks to this verification future. Registration starts with self=1 and attaches every replication worker; notifyAll passes a bool to vote, whose second positive notification crosses threshold 2; leaderLoop responds nil. The public future observation therefore corresponds to the source-identified eligibility defect. The necessity predicate is success implies eligible quorum, not equivalence; the independently declared input policy and real admission are correlated by operation ID. No response or property value is used to admit the scenario. Completion and sampling precede shutdown, and actual successful-path cleanup waits tracked leader workers before joining externally owned follower RPC pumps. The composed normative basis is the voter-derived quorum confirmation role of VerifyLeader, voter/nonvoter eligibility and the explicit voter filtering in other authority support. This supports the local accounting requirement rather than claiming this still-recently-elected leader already served stale data. No current correspondence issue found within this scope. Explained alternatives: Lease checking independently counts only voters and could cause later stepdown, but does not make the nonvoter callback an eligible vote in the completed verification. The older multi-bootstrap helper/API wording conflict is retained historically; this version uses single bootstrap and no longer relies on the helper.
